title: L1 — Decision record: Beacon beside OAC, not inside it (pin, license, operator decisions Q1-Q5)
body:
**Status:** ACTIONABLE NOW — planning/decision work outside product paths, no stage dependency (same reasoning as Epic K's K1, `docs/planning/STATUS.md` "Current stage")

**Source:** issue #165 workstreams L1 and L3; `[ADR-001 Boundary]`; `[DESIGN Non-goals]`; `[PLANNING-PROMPT §10]`; `oac-boundaries` #12

## Outcome
One decision record fixes the "Beacon beside OAC, not inside it" shape, pins one Beacon release, records its MIT license as an external, not-shipped service, and records the operator's answers to Q1-Q5 so no later task re-opens them.

## Operator decisions to record verbatim (already made, 2026-09-29)
- **Q1 → option (a), docs-only.** Memory IDs travel as ordinary text in `content[].text`. **No new spec content type.** Epic workstream L3 (spec touchpoint) is closed by this record with a "no spec change needed" note; no Stage 2 spec task is created for it. Cite `docs/planning/v0.1/05-interfaces.md` §3 only to show that nothing in the envelope/content model has to change.
- **Q2 → no `oac doctor` check** that reads harness MCP configuration files. Rationale: those files "hold other servers' credentials" (Beacon's own wording, `docs/cli/mcp-doctor.mdx`), and a Beacon detector would be OAC configuring or inspecting Beacon.
- **Q3 → yes, recommend Metadata-only privacy for OAC-enabled sessions, as a recommendation with rationale.** Scope it correctly (desk finding while breaking this epic down, re-check at the pinned tag): Beacon's `Metadata-only` is a **Beacon Cloud forwarding** mode (`beacon endpoint connect ... --privacy-mode metadata-only`), applied by a local Vector transform before upload. It does **not** change local capture: `runtime.jsonl` still holds redacted/sanitized/truncated content. Sources at commit `26581914`: `docs/security/retention-redaction.mdx` §"Forwarding implications", `cli/beacon/README.md` (Beacon Cloud section). So the recommendation is: Local mode (no forwarding) or, if Beacon Cloud forwarding is enabled, Metadata-only; the local-capture residual stays and goes to L4's threat rows.
- **Q4 → accept the scoping mismatch, documented, not solved.** Beacon memory is per resolved repository; OAC sessions are per `working_directory` (`docs/planning/decisions/C4-session-identity.md` §5).
- **Q5 → stay inside ADR-001.** No amendment, no OAC-injected context. Record the rejected reading (OAC as the shared context layer) and name the amendment route (`oac-evidence` §6, next free `ADR-001-A<n>`) without proposing it.

## Deliverables
- **New** `docs/planning/decisions/L1-beacon-memory.md`, mirroring the section shape of `docs/planning/decisions/K1-herdr-evaluation.md`: `## 0. Timebox`, `## 1. Decision` (the seven "in bounds" points from #165), `## 2. Pin`, `## 3. License`, `## 4. Operator decisions Q1-Q5`, `## 5. Rejected reading and amendment route`, `## 6. UNVERIFIED ledger` (the four items from #165, handed to L2), `## 7. Surface labels, boundary pass`, `## 8. Acceptance boxes`, `## 9. Cross-file updates in this change`, `## 10. Sources`. Quote the boundary lines listed in #165 verbatim.
- `docs/planning/PINS.md`: row `Beacon (external memory service)` in `## Pin table`, record `### Beacon (external memory service)` after `### herdr (test tooling)`, `Gates affected: none`, fixed (not floating), `**Last updated:**` bumped, pin-move checklist executed in the same commit (no gate invalidated). Pin candidate: release tag `v1.3.29` (tag object `72fd6643b5cd5c6ff6741f6016b3577654f61915` → commit `91e92216b79108475ba9b587d49c5ff3f7356fd8`); re-run `git ls-remote --tags https://github.com/Asymptote-Labs/agent-beacon` on the day and pin the latest release tag, and re-read every cited doc **at that tag** (the #165 facts were read at branch head `26581914`).
- `docs/planning/v0.1/07-repository-and-dependencies.md` §5: new heading `### External services — not shipped (outside this inventory)` directly after `### Dev/test tooling — not shipped (outside this inventory)`, same table columns, one Beacon row (MIT, "No — external service each harness connects to natively; OAC never imports, links, vendors, spawns or configures it").
- `docs/planning/v0.1/11-risks.md`: `### RISK-BEACON` under `## R5 — Low-impact / non-dependency risks` (floating upstream, MCP-era `2024-11-05`, UNVERIFIED items), and traceability rows starting at **53** (row 52 is the current last).
- `docs/planning/STATUS.md`: `**Last updated:**`, a bullet under `## Decisions landed`, and the open items under `## Open UNVERIFIED items`.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `test -f docs/planning/decisions/L1-beacon-memory.md` and `grep -c '^## ' docs/planning/decisions/L1-beacon-memory.md` ≥ 11
- [ ] `grep -n 'Beacon (external memory service)' docs/planning/PINS.md` hits both the pin-table row and the `###` record; the row's `Gates affected` cell reads `none`
- [ ] `grep -n 'External services — not shipped' docs/planning/v0.1/07-repository-and-dependencies.md` hits once; the row says MIT
- [ ] `grep -n 'RISK-BEACON' docs/planning/v0.1/11-risks.md docs/planning/STATUS.md` hits in both files
- [ ] Q1-Q5 each appear in §4 with the decision and rationale; §4 Q1 states "no spec change needed" and that no Stage 2 spec task exists for Beacon
- [ ] Every Beacon fact carries URL + tag/commit + retrieval date (`oac-evidence`); unresolved facts are labelled UNVERIFIED and mirrored in STATUS.md and `11-risks.md`
- [ ] `oac-boundaries` "Pre-commit self-check" run and recorded in §7
- [ ] No existing gate verdict, pin value, or ADR text changes: `git diff --name-only origin/main -- docs/planning/gates docs/planning/ADR-001.md docs/planning/ADR-001-AMENDMENTS.md` is empty; `git diff --name-only origin/main | grep -E '^(core|spec|adapters|cli|transports)/'` is empty
- [ ] `node scripts/check-skills.mjs`, `node scripts/check-herdr-containment.mjs`, `node scripts/check-fixture-manifest.mjs` still pass

title: L2 — Beacon desk research: close or carry the four UNVERIFIED items at the pinned tag
body:
**Status:** ACTIONABLE NOW (after #166) — desk leg only, no stage dependency, no harness needed

**Source:** issue #165 workstream L2 (desk leg); "UNVERIFIED (to be closed or listed in L1/L2)"

## Outcome
Each of the four UNVERIFIED items in #165 is confirmed, refuted, or explicitly carried open, from Beacon's own source and docs **at the tag L1 pinned**, and the operator-run live checklist for L3 is written.

## Deliverables
- `docs/planning/decisions/L1-beacon-memory.md`: new `## 11. Desk research (L2)` with one `###` per item, each ending in CONFIRMED / REFUTED / UNVERIFIED plus `path@tag` citations and retrieval date:
  1. Does Beacon's Claude Code capture (hooks / OTLP / poll) record the text of a `notifications/claude/channel` delivery, or only harness-visible prompt/tool events? Same question for a Codex session receiving `thread/queue/add` / `turn/start` input from an app-server client (Codex capture is `OTLP + hooks + poll`). Read `cli/beacon-hooks/` and the harness mappers at the tag.
  2. Memory item ID shape and stability, and the `get_memory` / `get_memory_context` result shape (`cli/beacon/internal/mcpserver/server.go`, the memory store schema). Is there a versioned response schema?
  3. Concurrent access to one `memory.db` from several harness sessions: documented locking model or not (storage engine, WAL, etc.).
  4. Config collisions: does Beacon's endpoint hook install or `beacon mcp connect` touch `~/.codex/config.toml` / Claude Code `settings.json` / `hooks.json` in a way that conflicts with OAC's planned launch paths (`docs/planning/v0.1/08-cli-and-deployment.md` §7 Claude launch, §9 Codex launch)?
- Same file: new `## 12. Live-verification checklist (operator-run, NOT RUN)` in the style of K1 §6 — steps, timebox, what to capture, redaction rules — which L3 executes.
- `docs/planning/STATUS.md` `## Open UNVERIFIED items` and `docs/planning/v0.1/11-risks.md` traceability rows (from 53 on, as L1 added them): each item marked CLOSED with citation or kept open with the narrowed wording (`oac-evidence` §5: never silently promoted).

## Acceptance

title: L3 — Beacon live leg (operator-run): what Beacon captures when a channel message lands in Claude Code and Codex
body:
**Status:** OPERATOR-RUN — not stage-blocked, but needs a human with a logged-in Claude Code and Codex and Beacon installed in Local mode. An agent in a cloud session without those skips this issue (same pattern as K1's live leg, #124).

**Source:** issue #165 workstream L2 (live leg); UNVERIFIED items 1 and 4

> Numbering note: #165's draft workstream "L3 — spec touchpoint" was closed by operator decision Q1 (docs-only, no new content type) and is recorded in L1 (#166). This key is reused for the live leg.

## Outcome
Observed, not inferred: what Beacon writes to `runtime.jsonl` (and whether memory candidates can later be drawn from it) when a peer message is delivered into a Beacon-instrumented Claude Code session and a Codex session; and whether Beacon's hook/plugin install changed any harness config file OAC's launch paths rely on.

## Deliverables
- Execute the checklist written by L2 in `docs/planning/decisions/L1-beacon-memory.md` §12, inside its timebox, at the L1-pinned Beacon tag, Beacon in **Local mode** (no Beacon Cloud, no SIEM forwarding).
- Deliver a synthetic channel message the way the Stage 1 spikes did (there is no OAC product yet): the G1/G5 throwaway channel server pattern for Claude (`docs/planning/gates/G1-result.md`; reconstructed server `tools/herdr/gate-servers/g5-channel.mjs`) and the G2/G5 app-server client pattern for Codex (`docs/planning/gates/G2-result.md`; `tools/herdr/gate-servers/g5-codex.mjs`). Message body contains a unique marker string and a fake secret-shaped token so redaction behaviour is observable.
- `docs/planning/decisions/L1-beacon-memory.md`: new `## 13. Live results (L3)` — per harness: harness version, Beacon version, whether the marker appears in `runtime.jsonl` (field names only plus a short **redacted** excerpt inline), whether the fake token was redacted, and a before/after hash of `~/.codex/config.toml`, Claude Code `settings.json` and `hooks.json`.
- Close or narrow UNVERIFIED items 1 and 4 in `docs/planning/STATUS.md` and `docs/planning/v0.1/11-risks.md` (rows from 53 on).
- **No fixture file is committed**: `docs/planning/gates/fixtures/` is reserved for the G1-G5 and D6 slugs (`docs/planning/gates/README.md` §"Naming convention"). Redacted excerpts go inline in §13.

title: L4 — Security: memory-reference doctrine and threat rows 21-23 in 06-security.md
body:
**Status:** ACTIONABLE NOW (after #166) — planning-package doc rows only. Normative text is L9 (Stage 2); proving tests are L10 (Stage 5).

**Source:** issue #165 workstream L4; `06-security.md` §2-§3, §8-§10, §13-§15; `oac-security-work` §1 (threat table template) and §3 (authenticated but untrusted)

## Outcome
The planning security doc states that a memory reference in a message, and anything a receiving harness later resolves through its own memory service, is authenticated-but-untrusted content that never appears in the machine-set provenance block, and the threat table carries the three Beacon-related threats with no blank proving-test cell.

## Deliverables
- `docs/planning/v0.1/06-security.md`
  - §2 / §3 (e): one doctrine paragraph — a memory reference (per L1 Q1, plain text in `content[].text`) is a sender claim; resolved memory is untrusted text to the receiving harness too; OAC never fetches, validates or renders it.
  - §8, §9, §10: one sentence each (or one in §10 covering both) — no memory ID or memory body is ever placed in Claude `meta` or the Codex header block; provenance stays machine-set from daemon state.
  - §13: note that an external memory/telemetry service capturing session history is outside the `working_directory` scoping OAC enforces (L1 Q4).
  - §14: rows **21** (memory reference or resolved memory treated as an instruction — prompt injection via memory), **22** (a peer cites a memory ID to lend false authority to an instruction), **23** (an OAC-delivered message is captured by an external memory/telemetry service: cross-project disclosure, secret leakage via `runtime.jsonl`, opt-in forwarding). All five columns filled. Proving tests: rows 21-22 name L10's Stage 5 scenario plus the existing G5/F11 provenance tests; row 23 is an explicit **open risk** (outside OAC's control) whose residual cell cites L1 Q3 (Local mode or Metadata-only forwarding; local capture remains) and the L2/L3 finding.
  - §15: update the row count ("twenty rows") and disposition; §20 "Cross-file updates in this change".
  - Use neutral wording in the rows ("an external memory service, e.g. Beacon per L1") so L9 can lift them into `spec/security.md` under the neutral-vocabulary ban.
- `docs/planning/v0.1/09-test-strategy.md` §12: rows 21-23 and the updated row count.
- `docs/planning/v0.1/11-risks.md`: `RISK-BEACON` gains the capture-side residual (row 23).
- `docs/planning/STATUS.md`: `**Last updated:**`.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `grep -cE '^\| (21|22|23) \|' docs/planning/v0.1/06-security.md` = 3 and the same command on `docs/planning/v0.1/09-test-strategy.md` = 3
- [ ] No §14 row has an empty cell: `awk -F'|' '/^\| [0-9]+ \|/{for(i=2;i<=7;i++) if($i ~ /^ *$/) print NR}' docs/planning/v0.1/06-security.md` prints nothing
- [ ] `grep -n 'twenty' docs/planning/v0.1/06-security.md docs/planning/v0.1/09-test-strategy.md` shows no stale row count

title: L5 — Docs: running OAC sessions beside Beacon, and what OAC does not do with memory
body:
**Status:** ACTIONABLE NOW (after #166) — planning docs only. There is **no `cli/` work**: operator decision Q2 removed the doctor check. Re-verification against the shipped CLI is L11 (Stage 6).

**Source:** issue #165 workstream L5; operator decisions Q1-Q4 as recorded in L1

## Outcome
An operator can read one section and run Claude Code and Codex with Beacon on both sides using only Beacon's documented commands and OAC's documented launch commands, and knows exactly what OAC does not do with memory.

## Deliverables
- `docs/planning/v0.1/08-cli-and-deployment.md`
  - New `## 20. Running beside an external memory service (Beacon)` after `## 19. Cross-reference block`, containing:
    - Prerequisites and a pointer to L1's pin (no version repeated — link, don't copy).
    - Beacon side: only Beacon's own commands at the pinned tag (the stdio `mcpServers.beacon` entry `beacon mcp serve --transport stdio`, or the plugin marketplace install), each cited `path@tag`.
    - OAC side: only the launch commands in §7 (Claude) and §9 (Codex), marked planned-not-built per this file's "Gate-verdict caveat".
    - Referencing memory across sessions (Q1): put the memory ID in the message text; the receiver looks it up through its own Beacon connection.
    - Privacy recommendation (Q3), scoped correctly: prefer Beacon Local mode; if Beacon Cloud forwarding is on for an OAC-enabled machine, use `--privacy-mode metadata-only`; state that local `runtime.jsonl` still captures delivered messages (redacted/sanitized), with the rationale and a pointer to L4 row 23.
    - Scoping mismatch (Q4): Beacon memory is per resolved repository, OAC sessions are per `working_directory`; peers in different checkouts see different memory. Documented, not solved.
    - "What OAC does not do": never calls, spawns, proxies or configures Beacon; never reads or writes `memory.db`; never attaches, injects, trims or summarizes memory; never holds Beacon Cloud or Jev credentials; Beacon's activity log is not a mailbox, presence or catch-up mechanism (`[DESIGN Delivery semantics]`, deferred offline mailboxes).
  - `## 6. \`oac doctor\` check list`: one sentence — doctor deliberately does not inspect harness MCP configuration for Beacon (Q2, with rationale).
  - `## 18. Cross-file updates in this change`: entry for this change.
- `docs/planning/v0.1/12-deferred.md` `## 2. Boundary, not backlog`: under "Shared context management", one sentence naming "OAC as a shared memory layer (storing, fetching, attaching or injecting memory such as Beacon's)" as boundary, not backlog, citing L1.
- `docs/planning/STATUS.md`: `**Last updated:**`.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `grep -n '^## 20. Running beside an external memory service' docs/planning/v0.1/08-cli-and-deployment.md` hits once
- [ ] Every `oac` command in §20 is in the §5 command table: `sed -n '/^## 20\./,$p' docs/planning/v0.1/08-cli-and-deployment.md | grep -oE '\boac [a-z-]+' | sort -u` ⊆ {`oac start`, `oac status`, `oac sessions`, `oac doctor`, `oac mcp-shim`}
- [ ] Every `beacon ...` command in §20 carries a `path@tag` citation at the L1 pin
- [ ] §20 contains no step where OAC calls, spawns or configures Beacon (reviewer checks against `oac-boundaries` #12 and the "What OAC does not do" list)
- [ ] `grep -n 'memory' docs/planning/v0.1/12-deferred.md` shows the new §2 sentence
- [ ] No `cli/` path touched: `git diff --name-only origin/main | grep -Ev '^docs/planning/'` is empty
- [ ] `node scripts/check-skills.mjs` passes

title: L6 — Mechanical check 11: no Beacon in product paths or workspace manifests
body:
**Status:** ACTIONABLE NOW — no dependency; mirrors K2 (#125)

**Source:** issue #165 epic acceptance criterion 3; ADR-001 boundaries (context management, credential reuse); `oac-boundaries` #12

## Outcome
A build-failing check that no Beacon identifier, tool name, store path or dependency reaches product code or a workspace manifest, so "Beacon beside OAC, not inside it" is enforced rather than just documented.

## Deliverables
- `.claude/skills/oac-boundaries/references/mechanical-checks.md`: new `# 11.` entry in the grep block, following checks 9-10's comment style, with status and scope notes. Pattern (case-insensitive), at minimum: `\bbeacon\b|beacon_|beacon-managed|agent-beacon|asymptote-labs|memory\.db|get_memory_context|search_memory|get_memory\b`. Scope: git-tracked files under `adapters/`, `core/`, `cli/`, `transports/`, `spec/`, plus root `Cargo.toml` / `Cargo.lock` if present. Since Q1 chose docs-only, there is **no** spec exception.
- `.github/workflows/boundary-lint.yml`: new step `Check 11 - no Beacon in product paths` using `git ls-files` over those paths piped to `rg` (same exit-code handling as checks 3 and 8). Zero tracked files prints `PENDING` and exits 0 — pending is not a pass, per `mechanical-checks.md`.
- `.claude/skills/oac-boundaries/SKILL.md`: no body change unless the Mechanical checks section enumerates checks by number; if it does, add 11.
